subject: Short customer-facing summary of DPA, subprocessors, and transfer safeguards
messages:
From: Maya Patel <m.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Request: short privacy summary for Procurement review

Hi Stephanie,

Procurement at Acme is asking for a concise, customer-friendly summary of Redwood's DPA, subprocessors, and how cross-border data transfers are handled for the Hosted API. They need something that our legal and procurement reviewers can circulate — single page or short bullets — plus any checklist items (SOC 2, subprocessor disclosure, encryption at rest/in transit) we should attach.

Can you send a one-page blurb we can attach to the SOW? Our internal timeline: final procurement review by 2027-01-05.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Attachment: acme-procurement-questions.pdf (procurement checklist)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <m.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short privacy summary for Procurement review

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the note and the timeline. Attached is a first-draft one-page summary for procurement (dpa-exec-summary-v1.docx). Key bullets in plain language (excerpt):

• What we process: Hosted API processes customer-supplied prompts and generates model outputs; we do not index or reuse customer prompts for model training unless a customer opts in.
• Data handling: All data in transit is encrypted (TLS); stored data is encrypted at rest by default. We retain request logs and telemetry per customer-configurable retention settings; customers can request deletion or extended retention for compliance.
• Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list; we only use subprocessors for hosting, observability, and managed storage. We notify customers of material changes and provide a data access point for the current list.
• Cross-border transfers: Transfers are protected by standard contractual safeguards, and customers can choose regional deployment (residency toggle) where available to keep data within a specific region.
• Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, encryption architecture summary, and our subprocessor map are available on request or via an authenticated link.

Action items:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme needs a signed DPA or a DPA + procurement SOW?
2) Do you want the residency toggle callout to include a short screenshot from the Console?

We included a short attachment and I’ve looped in Karthik (privacy lead) and Laura (solutions) to add technical language or vendor-specific notes.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: dpa-exec-summary-v1.docx (one-page customer-friendly blurb)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Patel <m.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short privacy summary for Procurement review

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 2:18 PM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> • Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list; we only use subprocessors for hosting, observability, and managed storage. We notify customers of material changes and provide a data access point for the current list.

Thanks — quick edits to keep this procurement-friendly and precise:

• Subprocessors (reworded): We publish a live subprocessor list and use subprocessors only for infrastructure (compute/storage), telemetry, and third-party auth. We follow a security review process before onboarding a subprocessor and promise 30 days notice for material additions; customers may request alternatives for regulated workloads (Dedicated or Private).
• Transfers: Clarify that transfers rely on SCCs or equivalent safeguards and that customers in regulated industries can opt for Dedicated/Private deployment or regional hosting in supported cloud regions.

I've attached the latest subprocessor extract (subprocessor-map-csv.csv) you can reference for the procurement packet. Also recommend adding a short sentence about our fallback/resilience policy (automatic model routing to a compatible variant, so the service remains available if a region loses capacity).

Karthik Iyer
Product Lead, Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: subprocessor-map-csv.csv (latest extract)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Patel <m.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short privacy summary for Procurement review

Adding one practical item from Solutions:

• Console residency toggle: We can include a screenshot and short how-to that shows how customers select a region for Hosted API instances (Console -> Settings -> Data Residency). If Acme prefers, we can also commit to deploying a Dedicated pool in a single region under a reserved capacity agreement.

Also attaching a SOC 2 excerpt that procurement typically asks for — we should send the redacted excerpt rather than full report at this stage.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: soc2-excerpt.pdf (redacted excerpt for procurement)

From: Maya Patel <m.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-12-29T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short privacy summary for Procurement review

Hi all —

This is very helpful, thanks. The one-page blurb plus the subprocessor extract and SOC 2 excerpt will cover our procurement checklist for initial review. Two quick asks before we circulate to Acme legal:

1) Can you provide a DocuSign-ready DPA link (or tell us whether you prefer to send signed DPA after SOW)?
2) We’ll need a short line confirming you do not use customer prompts to train models unless the customer opts in (please include exact wording we can paste into our SOW).

If you can send those by EOD Friday (2027-01-01 UTC), that would keep us on track for the 2027-01-05 procurement milestone.

Thanks — I’ll loop legal in once we have the final pieces.

Best,
Maya
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
Attachment: acme-procurement-questions.pdf (updated)
